$comment: The committed registry of ALWAYS-ON agent routines (role-lens review, ai-ops next-work). Every recurring scheduled lane is declared here with its cadence, the human who authorized it, what it may write, where it stops and escalates, and where its firing evidence lands. scripts/check-scheduled-routines.mjs holds this file against the heartbeat artifacts and the org roster; its header states honestly that it gates the DECLARATION and the EVIDENCE OF FIRING — it cannot read the live account scheduler. Transcribed FROM the live scheduler (list_triggers) on 2026-08-21, not from memory. One-shot self-reminders (send_later check-ins) are deliberately out of scope: they are ephemeral work-pacing, not standing lanes.
transcribedFrom: live scheduler, 2026-09-05 (re-transcribed on moving mac-lane-steward-duty-cycle to hourly and both self-session routines onto lane-deliver; mac-lane-tick added the same day — it is a launchd agent on the owner's Mac, not an account trigger, so it is declared from scripts/mac/install-launchd.sh rather than from list_triggers; earlier: 2026-08-21; 2026-09-13: the brain-cycle account trigger was created then deleted — list_triggers confirms none exists — and its row is kept awaiting-activation; 2026-09-13 (later): forward-build-cycle added as an ACTIVE self-session routine (trig_01XLv3hGCPob8qcEDsZJ2xM8) per the owner's explicit go to build the company forward continuously; the second brain-cycle trigger created that day was deleted again, so list_triggers still shows no brain-cycle trigger)

routines.authorizationEvidence: owner message in-session: 'Can you have an employee monitor and administrator for the Mac lane please' — the role was created in direct response, same day. Cadence 4h -> hourly on 2026-09-05, owner message: 'Need you to have a better system with local Mac lane cause this is not working and causing delay'. Delivery made EVENT-DRIVEN + KEEPALIVE on 2026-09-23 (owner decision): a heartbeat PR is delivered only on a NON-QUIET cycle (real Mac activity, a new/moved mac/* branch, a sim result, mail to ack, manifest drift, or an action taken) OR when the last heartbeat is >2h old (a time-based keepalive under the 3h cadenceToleranceHours); a quiet cycle within tolerance delivers nothing. The hourly WAKE (cron 24 * * *) is unchanged so new mac/* branches and mail are still reviewed within the hour. Owner directive 2026-09-23 ('build something that monitors the raise your hand function then apply what is needed for the agents to address or create new agent and or skill to fill that gap regardless if it's for any lane'): each cycle also runs the raised-hands skill — dispatch the blocker-dispatcher agent for the cloud lane, execute its dispatch plan, clear what was resolved, raise covering hands for the Mac's, bundle overdue owner hands once — and checks the raised-hands issue is fresh (<2h), re-running raised-hands.yml if not. Raise/clear/take ops ride the cycle's one lane:deliver batch.

Plus: opens a draft PR for every unmerged origin/mac/* branch, subscribes to it, reviews and lands it. Since 2026-09-06 it also carries the duties absorbed from the retired live-sync-loop-keeper: checks pending sim-requests (scripts/check-sim-requests.mjs), unread lane messages (scripts/check-lane-messages.mjs), and the age of artifacts/live-evidence/mac-run.json — when that file is >3 days stale it mails the Mac lane through lane:deliver.

routines.writeScope: artifacts/agent-heartbeats/mac-lane-tick.json (via lane:deliver, straight to SignalGrid_Alpha) and artifacts/sim-results/** + artifacts/live-evidence/** on mac/tick-<stamp> branches only; since 2026-09-24 (DR-056) also docs/agent/objective-state.json (the shared task state, rewritten whole ONLY when the decision changed) and at most one artifacts/sim-requests/objective-loop-*.json per tick (a request the tick can run, queued by scripts/objective-loop.mjs --write --deliver in step c', which runs AFTER the sim-request step so provenance is sampled on a clean tree) on the same mac/tick-<stamp> branch, plus ONE lane-deliver send per NEW escalation id (never per tick); never the code branches, never lane mail (only a person acks a message); since 2026-09-23 its heartbeat delivery passes --no-wake — the heartbeat is a staleness record the steward reads from the FILE and never carries cloud-addressed mail, so it must not post the mailbox-PR comment that wakes the cloud lane; real cloud mail rides a separate lane-deliver send that still wakes at once.

routines.trigger: launchd:com.signalgrid.build-tick (installed by scripts/mac/install-build-tick.sh on the owner's Mac; not an account trigger)
routines.binding: launchd user agent on the Mac lane's machine, running scripts/mac/build-tick.sh (which pins SignalGrid_Alpha's sha once per run with git ls-remote of the real remote and re-execs that sha's copy); the script runs a STAGED pipeline of headless `claude -p` sessions (scripts/mac/build-tick-stages.mjs holds the one stage table; tiers follow DR-047 and the DR-060 stage table): triage on sonnet, READ-ONLY by tool absence (--tools Read,Grep,Glob; no Bash, Edit or Write); build on haiku, sonnet or opus by the kind triage names (mechanical, code, judgment; an unknown kind resolves to opus); review on opus, READ-ONLY by tool absence; at most one fix on the build's own tier, then a second review. Each stage uses --output-format json and caps per the helper's table (wall clock, turns, and a budget cap and opus fallback model that are UNVERIFIED on subscription auth), never bypassPermissions, and no session has git or GitHub credentials in its environment. The script, not a session, does every outward act
routines.authorizationEvidence: owner in a Mac Claude Code session, 2026-09-29 (DR-061 answer b): asked 'Should the Mac start a build session by itself every few hours when the brain has a buildable task? This uses your Claude usage.' he chose 'Yes, build it (Recommended) — The brain builds its top task unattended and opens PRs.' After the auto-mode classifier refused the build as an unattended agent, he confirmed explicitly: 'Build it, I confirm — You explicitly approve an unattended Claude agent on this Mac with push + PR rights.' The PR-refresh step (below) pushes to other mac/* PR heads, which widens the write scope past this tick's own branches; the owner's covering instruction for that, verbatim (owner, in the Mac Claude Code session of 2026-10-01 (session_01XJMTVvCtYFZVkhK4K5nRdc), to the Mac lane): "Just get the merges done whatever it needs I'll approve." This row reads that instruction as covering exactly one thing: re-merging origin/SignalGrid_Alpha into the owner's own open mac/* PR branches (a fast-forward merge onto the head, never merging a PR itself), and nothing wider.
routines.writeScope: AFTER the pause check (a paused tick refreshes nothing) and BEFORE it picks a row it runs, once it lands (it is PR #1353, not on mainline yet; until then the tick logs that mainline has no pr-refresh.mjs and skips the refresh), mainline's scripts/mac/pr-refresh.mjs --max 1 (extracted from the mainline sha this run pinned, never a branch copy), which may push ONE fast-forward merge of origin/SignalGrid_Alpha onto ONE open mac/* PR head (never a mac/tick-* one), only after preflight and breadth exit 0 on that head; it also posts PR comments and raises hands, and its preflight runs that PR's code WITH credentials; a refresh failure or a refresh past its REFRESH_SECONDS cap never stops the build (the cap kills the refresh's whole process group, not only its launcher). The model sessions (build, fix) have only the tools Read, Edit, Write, Grep, Glob and Bash (--tools; no Task, Workflow, web, cron or messaging tool exists in them), and edit only their own clone <repo>.build (a `git clone --reference` of the person's repo with its own .git, so refs, config, stash and hooks are not shared with the person's checkout; its config rewritten and its tree reset to the pinned mainline sha every run) and a run directory under ~/Library/Caches/signalgrid/build-tick/runs/; triage and review edit nothing. Mainline is pinned ONCE per run (git ls-remote of the real remote, never a ref a session could repoint): the clone reset, the diff the reviewer reads, the changed-path list, the forbidden-path check, the landing classifier and an is-ancestor check before the push all use that one sha, and a run that cannot ask the remote does nothing ("skipped: origin unreachable"). Every script-side git call after a session ran goes through hooks-off git (a session can plant hooks) and reads the real objects (GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS=1 and a GIT_GRAFT_FILE that points at nothing, exported by the script, so a replace ref or an info/grafts a session planted cannot make diff, merge-base or status show a substitute), and the clone's config, info/exclude, info/attributes, replace refs and grafts are rewritten or deleted at run start, after each writing session and again before the push (a session can write them straight into the clone's .git, which the git deny list never sees); CI's frozen-lockfile install is the lockfile guard for tick PRs. The helper makes LOCAL commits in that clone and appends one cost-ledger line per stage to ~/Library/Caches/signalgrid/build-tick/ledger.jsonl (and the run directory's own copy); it never pushes. A mechanical (haiku) change, which is a writer rerun or a doc-only edit, may touch only docs/** (never a *-ratchet.json) and artifacts/sync/live-sync-manifest.json: the helper hands back any other diff and writes that change's commit message and PR body itself (DR-060: never Haiku). The SCRIPT pushes ONE branch per run, mac/build-row-<rowId>-<stamp> (first as an empty claim at the pinned mainline sha, then fast-forwarded to the session's commit only when preflight and breadth both exit 0 with their exact full verdict lines and a sentinel naming that sha, pushed BY SHA to the origin URL read before any session, from a clean tree whose HEAD is the commit the gates ran on), opens ONE PR through scripts/mac/gh-pr.mjs, and raises hands through lane-deliver batch (straight to SignalGrid_Alpha). Nothing in it merges or force-pushes, its push runs with git hooks off (the repo's local pre-push hook is deliberately not run, because a session can edit hooks; CI's frozen-lockfile install is the lockfile guard for tick PRs), and it never edits the person's working tree or refs or the lane tick's worktree (it only fetches the pinned sha's objects into the person's object store and prunes stale worktree registrations, and once, on first run after this change, removes the old <repo>.build worktree it replaces with a clone). Enforced by the environment, the deny list and the script, not an OS boundary: a session that deliberately wrote its own push route could still escape — a `pnpm exec`/`node` one-liner re-pointing git at ssh and the on-disk keys, or code this script's own preflight then runs with credentials (DR-061 rule 4 accepts that). The script refuses to land a change touching an owner-reserved or forbidden path, pauses itself (~/Library/Caches/signalgrid/build-tick/paused) when a session is broken (see escalationBoundary), and raises one hand for a run hung past HUNG_SECONDS, which scripts/mac/build-tick.sh derives from the refresh, the stage table and the preflight and breadth budgets (a typed hour count here would only drift).
routines.escalationBoundary: builds only objective-state.json tasks[] rows no remote branch or open PR names; an unreadable task list, branch list or PR list stops the run rather than building blind; a session that is itself broken PAUSES the tick, where broken (build-tick-stages.mjs sessionBroken) means its envelope names an API error (api_error_status set, terminal_reason api_error, or is_error without an error_max_* cap, which is what a logged-out CLI prints) or it died with no envelope on an exit other than 0 or the wall-clock cap, and a turn or time cap is a hand, not a pause; a broken triage pauses BEFORE any claim is pushed, so that row stays unclaimed, while a build, fix or review that breaks after the claim pauses the tick and leaves that row's claim branch for a person; the branch and PR lists are re-read right before the claim, and a row taken during triage is skipped; a triage that finds a row blocked on the owner, a lab, a tenant, hardware or Docker raises a hand (the objective loop parks AWAITING/BLOCKED rows only once #1216 lands) and keeps the claim; an unparseable triage is built on opus, and an unparseable or capped review is a reject (DR-047); a build or fix session that stops (hand.txt, read after each of them), changes nothing, leaves no commit message/PR files, touches anything a mechanical change may not (outside docs/** and the sync manifest), or whose change fails preflight or breadth raises a hand (DR-054) for the Mac lane and leaves its claim branch for a person; a helper that fails (cannot read or render a brief, a failed git command, any exception that is not a content hand) or writes no verdict PAUSES the tick instead of raising a hand that would claim a new row every run; a build or fix session that edited and then capped or broke is not committed (broken pauses, capped hands); four origin-unreachable runs in a row (git ls-remote or the sha fetch failing; such a run does nothing) raise a hand
routines.heartbeatPathReason: each run's outcome is a pushed mac/build-row-* branch with its PR, or a raised hand; the Mac being awake is already watched by mac-lane-tick's 5-minute heartbeat. ponytail: a loaded-but-never-firing job is not caught here — add a heartbeat if that happens once.
routines.awaitingReason: the launchd job is installed (bash scripts/mac/install-build-tick.sh) only after this row and scripts/mac/build-tick.sh land on SignalGrid_Alpha (the script re-execs mainline's copy, which must exist); the Mac lane flips this row to active in the same session it installs.

routines.trigger: awaiting-activation — a cloud self-session trigger is created via create_trigger only AFTER this active row lands on SignalGrid_Alpha AND a Slice-2 dry run is proven end-to-end (DR-032 registry-first bootstrap). A same-session activation on 2026-09-13 was created out of that order and REVERTED (trigger deleted) per Codex #705. Not a launchd agent.
routines.authorizationEvidence: owner directed the standing Brain Cycle in-session 2026-09-09: shared the '9 Architectures for Multi-Agent Systems' graphic with 'I'm looking for a 🧠 to operate things and each one of these repos I've shared will do the same thing in this graph', then chose 'Standing recurring cycle', 'once a day', and 'auto but does x amount of security and code check validation for bugs and other problems for the winner'. This 2026-09-09 message authorizes BUILDING the machinery (Slice 1, dormant). ACTIVATION was subsequently authorized by the owner on 2026-09-13 ('Activate it now'), so no further owner consent is pending; what remains before the trigger is created is the registry-first sequence (land the active row on SignalGrid_Alpha, prove a Slice-2 dry run, then create_trigger) per the awaiting-activation contract and DR-032 — a technical prerequisite, not an owner gate.
routines.writeScope: artifacts/brain-cycle/** (the per-cycle audit blackboard), artifacts/lane-messages/** and artifacts/agent-heartbeats/brain-cycle.json (heartbeat via scripts/lane-deliver.mjs onto a lane/cloud-mail-* branch, never the code branch); opens DRAFT PRs for winning autonomous-tier routes only (classifyDiff==autonomous). Never auto-merges; never opens a PR touching SAFETY_MACHINERY or OWNER_RESERVED surfaces (those escalate).
routines.escalationBoundary: escalates to the owner every owner-gated route, every tie, and every unrecognised/ambiguous tier; auto-OPEN (draft) is the ceiling and auto-MERGE is off (owner GREEN switch in docs/agent/brain-cycle-config.json, default false). Fail-closed halts (not ships): a stale brain (check-brain-freshness), an absent or ran:false expected lens, or an unverifiable surface stops the cycle.
routines.awaitingReason: Machinery ready and owner-authorized (2026-09-09, re-affirmed 2026-09-13 'Activate it now'). A same-session activation on 2026-09-13 was REVERTED (trigger deleted): it created the trigger BEFORE this active row reached SignalGrid_Alpha (a fire could not heartbeat — check-scheduled-routines fatals on a heartbeat for an awaiting routine) and before the dispatch->gauntlet->PR path was proven end-to-end. Re-activation follows the design order: land this row active on Alpha, prove a Slice-2 dry run, THEN create_trigger (DR-032; Codex #705). Activation is NOT yet mechanically landable and is Slice-3 ENGINEERING, not a runbook (BRAIN_CYCLE_DESIGN.md Slice 3): authorizedOn (2026-09-09) doubles as the gate's active-no-heartbeat clock, so a bare flip to active is already past the 168h bound (needs a gate activatedOn baseline, a scripts/** change); and lane-deliver writes only the heartbeat artifact and runs check-scheduled-routines PRE-commit without staging this file, while the gate FATALs on awaiting-activation + a heartbeat, so the first fire cannot atomically land its heartbeat and flip status (needs a dedicated activation path, not lane-deliver). create_trigger must still come AFTER the row and a proven Slice-2 dry run (registry-first). Until that Slice-3 code exists the row stays awaiting-activation, authorizedOn is NEVER overwritten (the 2026-09-13 go is in authorizationEvidence), and no trigger is created. awaitingSince (2026-09-09) is the watchdog baseline and is NOT reset to dodge the 30-day bound: if the bound is reached before activation lands, ACTIVATE, RETIRE the row with evidence, or ESCALATE — never restart the clock (DR-032; Codex #705, #708).

routines.trigger: awaiting-activation — no account trigger yet; a fresh-session-per-fire trigger is created via create_trigger only AFTER an EXPLICIT owner go for this cadence (no consent is inferred from a build/evaluation directive, exactly as the brain-cycle row requires). Neither the cloud lane nor any persistent session may self-authorize creating the account trigger. Not yet a trig_*.
routines.authorizationEvidence: The owner asked for the 2026-09-12 organization self-evaluation ('make sure everything in this project is being worked on and has eyes on it ... through the proper channels'); its pipes reader found ten Dependabot PRs (#352-#361) open 11 days with CI never run and 'no roster role, routine, backlog row or LOOP line owns the monthly queue' (docs/agent/ORG_SELF_EVALUATION_2026-09-12.md row 6), and named the fix as 'roster row for the monthly queue'. This record-hygiene pass (docs/agent/EVIDENCE.md, 2026-09-12) executes exactly that named fix. `.github/dependabot.yml` sets `schedule.interval: monthly` for both its npm ecosystem groups, so the underlying QUEUE this routine watches is monthly and already running on GitHub; the CRON here is the CHECK cadence, and it is weekly rather than monthly on purpose — see the cron note below.
routines.writeScope: Its only repository write is its own heartbeat at `artifacts/agent-heartbeats/dependabot-queue-review.json` each cycle; it has NO merge authority and no other write scope — it REVIEWS and TRIAGES Dependabot's own PRs and ESCALATES every merge to the owner; it never auto-merges. Dependabot PRs change `package.json`/`pnpm-lock.yaml`, which `check-owner-gated-surfaces.mjs` treats as safety-machinery-adjacent, so the merge stays an owner decision regardless of green CI. It never edits `.github/dependabot.yml`, `pnpm-lock.yaml` by hand outside a Dependabot PR, or any file `check-owner-gated-surfaces.mjs` classifies SAFETY_MACHINERY/OWNER_RESERVED. Owned by the `devex-tooling-engineer` role (docs/agent/org-roster.json, docs/ORG_CHART.md:91): 'A gate changes, or one is suspected of passing vacuously' already covers a lockfile-changing PR; this row adds the recurring queue-check that role was missing.
routines.escalationBoundary: Escalates to the owner only for a major-version Dependabot PR that needs code changes to pass, or a run stuck in `action_required` needing the owner's one-time workflow approval (docs/OWNER_ACTIONS.md); a quiet week with nothing new and no PR older than its tolerance sends no owner message. It never merges any Dependabot PR itself, green or not — every merge is escalated to the owner.
routines.heartbeatPathReason: When active, the routine writes a heartbeat to this path each review cycle so a silent stop (a disabled trigger or a dead session) is distinguishable from a quiet successful week with nothing to review — a silent absence is not. No heartbeat file exists yet because the routine is still awaiting-activation.
routines.awaitingReason: Declared in this pass to close the gap the 2026-09-12 self-evaluation found; the account trigger is deliberately not created here because creating a recurring fresh-session cadence requires an EXPLICIT owner go (no consent is inferred from a build/evaluation directive), per the awaiting-activation contract this registry already uses for brain-cycle. Neither the cloud lane nor a persistent session may self-authorize it.
routines.cronNote: Dependabot's own schedule is `.github/dependabot.yml`'s `interval: monthly` — this registry's `cronIntervalHours` (scripts/check-scheduled-routines.mjs) can only read every-N-minutes, hourly, every-N-hours, daily, or weekly-single-weekday shapes; it has no monthly primitive, and an unparseable cron on a non-retired routine fails this gate's own self-test floor. So the cron above is WEEKLY (Monday 09:00 UTC), not monthly: it checks the monthly-generated queue often enough that an open PR is never unreviewed for the 11 days the self-evaluation found, which is a tighter bound than monthly would give and the one the finding actually calls for.

routines.authorizationEvidence: owner message in-session 2026-09-13: 'I want you to continue to always have everyone building the company ... the system aka brain keeps everything running no matter what I'm currently chatting with you or ask you do something else.' This is an explicit go for STANDING autonomous operation (not a per-feature build directive), so a self-session cloud trigger (trig_01XLv3hGCPob8qcEDsZJ2xM8) was created the same day; self-session so it inherits the operating session's push + GitHub-PR + merge path — the capability the retired fresh-session nightly-build-agent (trig_01WaoZcckmBjv5Pqs8hGNhFS) never had. Registry-first order: this active row lands on SignalGrid_Alpha well before the trigger's first fire (2026-09-14T15:00Z). 2026-09-29: the owner asked in-session why the brain was not building ("Please build the whole system using the brain why isn't this happening as I expected") and chose "Every 2h, whole backlog" when offered daily/every-2h/every-6h — so this routine now fires every two hours (10 */2 * * *, re-transcribed from the live scheduler after update_trigger) and works the whole cloud-buildable backlog, not only tasks[0..2].
routines.writeScope: claude/build-* code branches (ONE bounded product item per fire, opened as a PR to SignalGrid_Alpha for OWNER review/merge — the harness structurally blocks agent self-merge of product PRs), docs/BUILD_BACKLOG.md item status via that PR — and, since 2026-09-24 (DR-056), the item it picks is READ from docs/agent/objective-state.json tasks[0..2] first (the ranked company queue from docs/COMPANY_BUILD_PLAN.md "## Global backlog", resolved to real executors) and, since 2026-09-29 (owner: "whole backlog"), when none of those is cloud-buildable it takes the next open Global-backlog row this lane can build end to end (no live lab, no Swift toolchain or device, no owner decision, not already an open PR) instead of heartbeating quiet; the recorded verdict is trusted only while the mac-lane-tick heartbeat (artifacts/agent-heartbeats/mac-lane-tick.json) is within the state's staleAfterHours AND names that verdict — otherwise the state reads unknown and the fire escalates instead of building on it; it may groom either backlog document by PR and the next Mac tick re-derives; it never writes the state file, and artifacts/agent-heartbeats/forward-build-cycle.json (heartbeat via scripts/lane-deliver.mjs onto a lane/cloud-mail-* branch, never the code branch). A purely autonomous-tier gate/doc/fossil-figure fix may self-merge under DR-037; it NEVER self-merges a product / launch-profile / launch-claims-gate / publication-boundary change.
routines.escalationBoundary: escalates to the owner only a genuine product decision (a new vertical / platform / hardware surface = DR-020) or a physical action he alone can take; a fire with nothing cleanly actionable builds nothing and heartbeats 'quiet' — no owner message. Runs in the operating session, so every fire is owner-supervisable.
